summary.text: 会 is the simplified form of 會, used for meeting, gathering, and an organization. Its visible 人 and 云 shapes come from later cursive writing, not an original “person and cloud” construction.

formation.text: 会 is a derived graphic form of 會. One analysis of 會 reads its early construction as 合 with a vessel-like element, suggesting parts fitted together; Xu Shen’s older account instead analyzes 亼 and an abbreviated 曾. The precise object and original sense remain uncertain.

components.text: 人 is visible in the upper part of 会 because this shape developed through cursive writing. It is not supported as a historical semantic or pictorial component.
云 is visible in the lower part of 会 because this shape developed through cursive writing. It is not supported as a historical semantic or phonetic component.

history.text: The graph 会 arose in cursive writing as a variant of 會, became common in later regular script, and was adopted as the simplified form. Its modern division into 人 and 云 should not be projected back onto the ancient graph.
Early forms of 會 have been analyzed as 合 with a vessel-like element; another historical analysis describes 亼 and an abbreviated 曾. Accounts differ over the central shape and the object it represents.

uncertainties.text: A fragmentary oracle-bone phrase 會我 may mean “meet,” but the reading is tentative. The reported bronze and Warring States examples attest meeting or joining, yet do not show whether a vessel or lid sense came first or establish a path from “fit together” to “meet.”
No phonetic role is established for 云 in 会. Historical pronunciation records concern 會 itself and do not give a sound comparison between 云 and 会.

senses.period: Warring States and later securely reported; earlier oracle-bone use tentative
senses.text: Reported bronze and Warring States examples use 會 for meeting at a place, joining ideas, and meeting in alliance. A fragmentary oracle-bone example may have the sense “meet,” but that reading is tentative.
会 is also a noun meaning a meeting or gathering. In Japanese, え is recorded for a gathering, especially a religious assembly, in an early ninth-century text.
会 also means an organization or association. The development of this sense from “meeting” or “gathering” is not dated here.

senses.period: historical; chronology relative to meeting unresolved
senses.text: Historical dictionary citations attest 會 as a noun meaning “lid” or “cover.” This sense fits some proposed readings of the graph’s vessel-like forms, but does not prove that interpretation or establish which sense came first.

developments.text: The noun “meeting” plausibly relates to the verb “meet,” but the attestations do not document when or how that shift occurred.

limitations.text: The earliest secure dating of “meet” or “assemble” relative to “lid” or “cover” is unresolved. A connection from fitting a lid to joining or meeting remains an interpretation rather than a demonstrated sequence.

overview.text: 会 is the simplified form of 會 and means to meet, gather, or a meeting. Its 人-and-云 appearance reflects later cursive writing, rather than an original “person and cloud” construction.

Pictogram (象形). The upper part and the lower part of the character, on the basis of the original versions, can be unified into 合 (two open mouths) with a food container in the middle; this character means both "bring together" (e.g., bring together people to discuss, putting a lid on a vessel) and "close, shut". The top of the character resembles 食, but it's connected to another mouth at the bottom of the character. The food container could be a 膾 /脍 (kuài), an ancient container for raw fish and finely minced/chopped meat.
Most of the pronunciations are ultimately cognate, derived from a root meaning "to join, to come together ~ to meet, to gather ~ to match, to fit ~ to understand". Perhaps related to 合 (OC *kuːb, *ɡuːb, “to match”) ~ 蓋 (OC *kaːbs, *kaːb, *ɡaːb, “lid”).
However, Min Nan ē instead derives from 解 (OC *kreːʔ, *kreːs, *ɡreːʔ, *ɡreːs, “to understand”) (Yang, 2001).

evidence.field: 形義通解；字形分類；出土用例
evidence.text: The database describes 會 in oracle-bone and bronze forms as 合 plus a container-like element: a lid covering a vessel and its contents, with the proposed original sense ‘fit together’. It reports oracle-bone 《合集》1030正「會我」 as a damaged, uncertain possible ‘meet/assemble’ use; bronze inscription 𠫑羌鐘「入長城，先會于平陰」 uses it for meeting at a place. The database also reports a bronze form with 彳 in some inscriptions and interprets it as meeting on a road. Warring States bamboo texts use 會 for joining, e.g. 郭店《語叢一》36 「所以會天道人道也」. These are separate records of graphic analysis and lexical uses; the oracle-bone ‘meeting’ reading is explicitly tentative.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：會

evidence.text: The article says oracle-bone forms grouped as 會 include three types: one from 合 plus 皿, and two from 合 plus a 日-like or frame-like middle element. It treats the 日/frame shapes as likely one graphic type, while reviewing differing earlier cataloguing decisions. The available search result gave the article’s own text, but opening the PDF returned an access/internal error, so its detailed argument and later sections were not inspected.
evidence.title: 吳品婕：《「合」與「會」甲骨金文用法重探》

evidence.field: 異體字 A01840-001; 會 variant entry
evidence.text: The dictionary identifies 会 as a variant of 會 and says the 会 shape arose in cursive writing, was used widely in later common regular-script writing, and was adopted in the PRC simplified-character list. Thus 会 is historically a graphic simplification/variant of 會, not an ancient 人+云 construction. The same entry records variant pronunciations guì, kuài, huǐ and huì for 會.
evidence.title: [A01840] 會 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: The page quotes Xu Shen’s 《說文》: 「會，合也。从亼从曾省。曾，益也。」 This is a historical lexicographic analysis: ‘combine/meet’, from 亼 and an abbreviated 曾, with 曾 explained as ‘increase’. The modern paleographic account on the same page instead analyzes early forms through 合 and a vessel/lid image. These are distinguishable accounts and the 《說文》 component explanation does not by itself confirm the vessel interpretation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：會

evidence.field: 《廣韻》 readings and Middle Chinese categories
evidence.text: The page records 會 fanqie 黃外 and 古外, both 去聲, 蟹攝泰韻合一; the initials are 匣 (voiced guttural) and 見 (voiceless velar), corresponding to distinct readings. Its table lists modern Mandarin huì and kuài. The repository Baxter–Sagart TSV, checked locally, has exact rows for 會: huì / Middle Chinese hwajH / Old Chinese *m-kˤop-s for ‘meeting; have a meeting’; another huì form *ɦʷˤajs is an Eastern Han transcription gloss; and kuài / kwajH / *kˤop-s for ‘calculate; calculation’. These repository spellings have been preserved exactly and kept sense-distinct. No claim is made that either reading represents the pronunciation of a putative component in 会.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：會

evidence.source: Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction appendix (secondary rendering of dataset)
evidence.text: The inspected table gives the meeting reading as Middle Chinese hwajH and Old Chinese *m-kˁop-s, gloss ‘come together’, and warns that this appendix is outdated relative to Baxter and Sagart’s 2014 book. The local structured TSV independently checked for this task uses *m-kˤop-s and *kˤop-s for its separate rows. evidence.source: 字通 via Kotobank / 日本国語大辞典
evidence.field: 會 character account and Japanese lexical attestation
evidence.text: 字通 presents the traditional character 会 as 會 and analyzes its older form as a covered cooking vessel, with a lower steamer and upper lidded vessel; it interprets the lid’s fitting as a semantic bridge to ‘fit/meet’. It says the meeting sense appears in oracle-bone/bronze forms and, more specifically, that use of 會 for ‘meeting’ is visible in the Warring States/early regional-state period and Qin and Xu bronzes. This is a source’s account, not independently settled proof of the vessel identification. Separately, the Japanese kun reading/word え ‘gathering, especially a religious assembly’ is dated in 日本霊異記 (810–824), with an example 「会を設けて供養しき」; this records a Japanese lexical use, not the origin of the graph.
evidence.title: 会(カイ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.field: Bronze and Warring States lexical attestations
evidence.text: For graphic development versus word history, the page reports a possible oracle-bone meeting use in 《合集》1030正, a bronze meeting use in 𠫑羌鐘 「入長城，先會于平陰」, and Warring States bamboo examples for bringing things/ideas together and treaty meeting. It also reports another bronze use for an account/record book in 訓匜. These distinct senses should not be treated as a chronology inferred from modern dictionary gloss order; the inscriptions provide separate attestation contexts.

evidence.field: Detailed explanation; citations and noun senses
evidence.text: The dictionary cites early received-text senses for ‘assemble/meet’ including 《詩·小雅·車攻》「會同有絳」 and 《詩·唐風·杕杜》「會言近止」, and later historical narrative examples including 《史記·廉頗藺相如列傳》 meeting at the border and 《史記·陳涉世家》 accounting/calculation usage. It separately lists the noun ‘lid/cover’, citing 《儀禮·士喪禮》 and 《儀禮·士虞禮》 for opening the 會. These establish attested lexical senses in cited texts but do not establish which sense chronologically preceded the other without dating and textual-history analysis.

evidence.text: The dictionary’s component connections for 會 are 合, 口, 𠓛 (container lid), and 彳 in certain bronze variants. evidence.source: 字通 via Kotobank / 日本国語大辞典
evidence.field: 會 character account and Japanese lexical attestation
evidence.text: 字通 presents the traditional character 会 as 會 and analyzes its older form as a covered cooking vessel, with a lower steamer and upper lidded vessel; it interprets the lid’s fitting as a semantic bridge to ‘fit/meet’. It says the meeting sense appears in oracle-bone/bronze forms and, more specifically, that use of 會 for ‘meeting’ is visible in the Warring States/early regional-state period and Qin and Xu bronzes. This is a source’s account, not independently settled proof of the vessel identification. Separately, the Japanese kun reading/word え ‘gathering, especially a religious assembly’ is dated in 日本霊異記 (810–824), with an example 「会を設けて供養しき」; this records a Japanese lexical use, not the origin of the graph.
evidence.title: 会(カイ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.field: Bronze and Warring States lexical attestations
evidence.text: For graphic development versus word history, the page reports a possible oracle-bone meeting use in 《合集》1030正, a bronze meeting use in 𠫑羌鐘 「入長城，先會于平陰」, and Warring States bamboo examples for bringing things/ideas together and treaty meeting. It also reports another bronze use for an account/record book in 訓匜. These distinct senses should not be treated as a chronology inferred from modern dictionary gloss order; the inscriptions provide separate attestation contexts.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：會

evidence.field: Detailed explanation; citations and noun senses
evidence.text: The dictionary cites early received-text senses for ‘assemble/meet’ including 《詩·小雅·車攻》「會同有絳」 and 《詩·唐風·杕杜》「會言近止」, and later historical narrative examples including 《史記·廉頗藺相如列傳》 meeting at the border and 《史記·陳涉世家》 accounting/calculation usage. It separately lists the noun ‘lid/cover’, citing 《儀禮·士喪禮》 and 《儀禮·士虞禮》 for opening the 會. These establish attested lexical senses in cited texts but do not establish which sense chronologically preceded the other without dating and textual-history analysis.
evidence.title: 會 huì、kuài、kuò - 汉典

evidence.text: The dictionary’s component connections for 會 are 合, 口, 𠓛 (container lid), and 彳 in certain bronze variants. It does not identify 人 or 云 as ancient components of 會, and its reading table concerns 會 itself. The local Baxter–Sagart dataset has no row for 云 in this query and no independent component reading data establishing 云 as the phonetic of 会. Therefore the dossier’s 人+云 mnemonic/analysis is unsupported as a historical account; the graph 会 is a later cursive-derived form of 會.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：會

evidence.text: This Hong Kong educational resource explains early 會 as the lower part of a 甗 steamer, its perforated partition in the middle, and a lid above; it says the graph depicts cooking vessels being fitted together. This is a specific vessel-identification proposal and conflicts in detail with CUHK’s more general vessel/lid/container interpretation and with Xu Shen’s component analysis. The page lists forms for oracle, bronze, seal, and standard scripts, but their images were not visually inspected here.
evidence.title: 字源考釋 - 會

evidence.text: The government character database records 會 U+6703 and gives Mandarin readings guì, kuài, huǐ, huì; it also records Taiwan Hakka and Taiwanese readings including ē, hē, huē, kuè. These are modern pronunciation records, not evidence of the ancient shapes or of a phonetic component in simplified 会.
evidence.title: 字形資訊 - [會] 1-6444 - 全字庫 CNS11643 (2024)

evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨、金文及戰國用例
evidence.text: The entry describes early 會 as 合 plus a vessel-like element: 口 is interpreted as a container, 𠓛 as its lid, and the middle as contents, yielding a proposed original sense ‘fit together’. It also reports bronze forms with 彳 as meeting on a road. The entry cites a fragmentary oracle-bone 《合集》1030正「會我」 as a *possible* meeting use; a bronze inscription on 𠫑羌鐘,「入長城，先會于平陰」, for meeting at a place; a bronze 訓匜 use for a legal account register; and Warring States bamboo uses for joining ideas and meeting in alliance. These are source-reported interpretations and attestations, not a proven semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：會

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK), quoting 《說文解字》
evidence.text: The page quotes Xu Shen’s account:「會，合也。从亼从曾省。曾，益也。」It separately displays categories for seal, bronze, oracle-bone and bamboo-slip forms. Xu Shen’s component analysis is a historical lexicographic account; it does not independently establish the modern vessel-and-lid interpretation. The entry also lists 合, 口, 𠓛 and, in some bronze forms, 彳 as related components.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：會

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry classifies 会 as a variant of 會. It says 会 arose in running/cursive writing, was widely used in later informal regular script, and was adopted in the PRC simplified-character list. This supports a later graphic simplification history for 会, rather than an ancient 人+云 construction.
evidence.title: [A01840] 會 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: 《廣韻》反切 and Middle Chinese categories
evidence.text: The entry records two 會 fanqie spellings, 黃外 and 古外, both 去聲 and 蟹攝泰韻合一, with initials 匣 and 見 respectively. They represent distinct readings of 會. The page gives modern Mandarin readings huì and kuài. It provides no basis here for treating 云 as a sound component of 会.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：會

evidence.source: 吳品婕, via National Chengchi University repository search result
evidence.field: Article summary on oracle-bone and bronze shapes
evidence.text: The search result reports that the article groups oracle-bone forms assigned to 會 into three types: 合 plus 皿, and two types with a 日-like or frame-like middle element. It notes prior differences in cataloguing and says later ancient forms may change an oracle-bone 口 element into 日. The PDF itself could not be opened in this session, so the detailed argument was not checked.
evidence.title: 吳品婕：《「合」與「會」甲骨金文用法重探》

evidence.field: Old Chinese reconstruction appendix entry for 會
evidence.text: The inspected search result gives the meeting reading as Middle Chinese hwajH and Old Chinese *m-kˁop-s, and states that its appendix is outdated relative to the 2014 book. The supplied dossier reports the local structured Baxter–Sagart TSV’s exact forms as *m-kˤop-s for the meeting reading and *kˤop-s for the separate calculation reading. These spellings differ in notation; they are retained as separate source renderings, not merged or silently corrected.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The Academia Sinica evolution page exposed only a skeletal page listing script stages; no glyph images were visually inspected. The NCCU paper’s PDF open failed, so only its search-result passage was usable; its full argument remains unreviewed.

The early graph’s central shape is interpreted differently across sources: a generic vessel/lid with contents, a cooking vessel/甗 assembly, and Xu Shen’s 亼 plus abbreviated 曾. The exact depicted object and whether the graph originally depicted a food steamer remain disputed or insufficiently demonstrated by the inspected material.

The oracle-bone 《合集》1030正 «會我» interpretation is explicitly tentative and the text is fragmentary. A secure earliest dated semantic use of ‘meet/gather’ versus a separate lid/container use was not established. The claimed ‘meeting’ bronze attestation is a secondary database report; inscription plates were not inspected.

The sources do not demonstrate a sound component in 會 or a historical phonetic role for 云 in 会. No independent pronunciation evidence for 云 was used, and 会’s derivation from cursive 會 makes a 人+云 origin implausible as graphic history.

Possible semantic extension from fitting a lid to joining/meeting is an interpretation, not a fully documented chronology. The dated record supports separate container/lid and meeting senses, but does not establish the path or direction of semantic development.

Modern Mandarin huì and kuài, Cantonese wui6 (from dossier), and Taiwanese ē forms represent distinct reading traditions/senses. The proposed Min Nan ē derivation from 解 was not independently verified from a primary dialectological source; a secondary search result mentioned it, but its supporting work was not inspected.

The outdated secondary Baxter–Sagart appendix prints *m-kˁop-s; the local structured dataset prints *m-kˤop-s. These notation differences are preserved. The KUài ‘calculate’ reading has its own *kˤop-s row and should not be conflated with the meeting reading.
No candidate image met the requirement for verified direct image URL, exact form identity and reusable provenance in this browsing session; therefore no glyph image is proposed.
The Xiaoxuetang record page did not expose its form labels or glyphs here, so its specific supplied labels and images could not be vetted or selected. The direct CUHK form links also failed to fetch.

The early central shape and depicted object remain disputed: the CUHK vessel-and-lid explanation, the reported 皿 / 日-like form groupings in the article search result, and Xu Shen’s 亼 plus abbreviated 曾 analysis are not identical accounts. The exact object is not established by the pages inspected.

The oracle-bone 《合集》1030正 «會我» interpretation is explicitly tentative and fragmentary. The bronze and Warring States attestations were available through a secondary database account; inscription plates were not inspected directly.
A semantic path from fitting a lid to meeting or gathering is a proposal rather than an established dated sequence. The listed inscriptional uses do not prove which sense came first.

The dossier reports local Baxter–Sagart TSV readings, but this invocation did not inspect the local file. The secondary appendix notation *m-kˁop-s differs from the dossier’s local *m-kˤop-s; that discrepancy remains unadjudicated here.

The inspected pages support no 人+云 analysis for 会 and no phonetic role for 云. No sourced component-pronunciation comparison for 云 was established; there is no supported sound component in the proposed 会 analysis to compare with 会’s huì reading.

limitations.text: The early forms of 會 have been interpreted as 合 combined with a vessel and lid, but the central shape and the object it depicts remain disputed. The fragmentary oracle-bone example «會我» is only a possible use meaning “meet”; the available evidence does not establish a dated sequence from a vessel or lid sense to meeting. The later form 会 is recorded as a cursive-derived variant of 會, rather than an ancient 人-and-云 construction.
